 Advertisement Oklahoma gubernatorial candidates Munson, Mazzei split on minimum wage hike
 Oklahoma’s two major-party gubernatorial candidates are split on raising the minimum wage, which is still $7.25 an hour.
 Advertisement Updated: 10:51 PM CDT Oct 25, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Chantelle Navarro Anchor Oklahoma gubernatorial candidates Munson, Mazzei split on minimum wage hike
 Oklahoma’s two major-party gubernatorial candidates are split on raising the minimum wage, which is still $7.25 an hour.
 Updated: 10:51 PM CDT Oct 25, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Chantelle Navarro Anchor Oklahoma is one of 20 states where the minimum wage remains at $7.25, and the two major-party candidates for governor are split on whether to raise it. 
 IMPORTANT ELECTION INFORMATION: Finding Your Polling Place | Finding Your Sample Ballot | Absentee Ballot Voting | Early Voting | Full List of Races | Meet Candidates Across the State | Who is Mike Mazzei? | Who is Cyndi Munson? 
 Advertisement Democrat Cyndi Munson and Republican Mike Mazzei talked about the possibility of raising the minimum wage, which remains at the federal rate and hasn't changed since 2009. 
 That equals about $15,000 a year before taxes for someone who works full time. 
 "What would be your thoughts on raising the minimum wage?" KOCO's Chantelle Navarro asked. 
 "No, no. Next question," Mazzei said. 
 "Not even just a little bit? There was a state question earlier this year, so there had to be some want for it," KOCO's Dacoda Wahpekeche said. 
 "I'm a small business owner. It's a bad idea. All the data, if you're an economics follower like me, shows that it actually depresses jobs for minorities. The people of Oklahoma soundly voted against it. I do not support any increases in the minimum wage," Mazzei said. 
 >> WATCH FULL VIDEO BELOW: Meet Oklahoma gubernatorial candidate Mike Mazzei 
 The only pay raise Mazzei advocates for in his campaign is for teachers. 
 State Question 832 was a citizen-led initiative that would have raised the minimum wage to $15 an hour by 2029. It would have then been tied to future increases to the cost of living. 
 Oklahoma voters rejected it. 
 "I do support increasing the minimum wage. Many of the economic challenges families are facing right now is because they're simply not making enough money. A person, you know, who wants to rent a one-bedroom apartment and has just basic bills that they have to pay around utilities and groceries and put gas in the car, at minimum, has to make $14.45 an hour in order to afford those basic necessities," Munson said. 
 >> WATCH FULL VIDEO BELOW: Meet Oklahoma gubernatorial candidate Cyndi Munson 
 In 2025, Munson wrote a House bill that would have also set the minimum wage to $15 an hour. But it didn't move out of committee. 
 It was what she called a "clean minimum wage," and she said she wants to push for it day one of becoming governor. 
 "What I mean by clean minimum wage is just increasing the wage and not tying it to inflation or removing exemptions like the state question did, and in my state of the state address, I will ask the legislature to come together and work on increasing the minimum wage," Munson said.
